title: Magnitude 7.3 earthquake quake strikes off Mexico coast
facts: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake occurred off the southern coast of Mexico on Friday, July 17, 2026.
The earthquake struck at 08:49 local time near the fishing town of Puerto Madero, Mexico.
The United States Geological Survey determined the earthquake occurred at a depth of 15.2 kilometers.
Mexican Navy Secretary Admiral Raymundo Morales confirmed there was no serious damage reported from the earthquake.
The US Tsunami Warning System recorded tsunami waves measuring 0.3 meters above tide level in Puerto Madero and Chiapas.
Tsunami wave activity lasted 12 minutes in Puerto Madero and 28 minutes in Chiapas.
Governor Salomón Jara Cruz confirmed that the earthquake was felt with moderate intensity across Oaxaca.
Governor Eduardo Ramírez ordered the suspension of public administrative activities in the state of Chiapas.
Tremors from the earthquake triggered building evacuations across Guatemala and El Salvador.
Multiple aftershocks with magnitudes ranging between 4.7 and 6 were recorded following the main event.
Guatemalan President Bernardo Arévalo deployed national emergency management personnel following a 5.6 magnitude tremor in Quetzaltenango.
The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration forecast potential waves under 0.3 meters for several Central and South American countries.
The earthquake produced no initial fatalities across Mexico and Guatemala.
Mexican authorities instructed residents to stay away from Pacific beaches following the initial tremor.
The US Tsunami Warning System lifted its tsunami threat advisory several hours after the earthquake.
